_about: The English pages that are localised. Everything else stays as it is: the legal pages (privacy, terms, abuse) are English-only on purpose - a machine translation of a legal text is worse than the original - and pages that are redirects, the Worker's own fallbacks, the live status board and the webapp are not marketing copy. Links from a localised page to an unlisted page go to the English one. `node scripts/i18n-web.mjs check` fails on any English .html page under apps/web/public that is in neither `pages` nor `englishOnly` (each with its reason), outside the generated language folders and the `ownI18n` trees, so a new page cannot ship English-only by accident.

englishOnly.why: legal text: a machine translation of a legal text is worse than the original
legal text: a machine translation of a legal text is worse than the original
legal text (notice-and-action, DMCA): a machine translation of a legal text is worse than the original
the Worker's own fallback, served at whatever path was missed (no /<lang>/ route)
the Worker's own pre-launch gate page, served in place of any path
the Worker's own fallback for app links (/join, /share, /voici-sign-in ...), served at the link's own path, never under /<lang>/; its sentences are set by its inline script
short-link chooser (a code that names more than one app), a utility page filled by its script, noindex; not localised yet
the live status board, operational data rather than marketing copy
Studio download page the Worker serves at /studio; not localised yet (it would need a /<lang>/studio route)

ownI18n.why: the webapp, localised at runtime from i18n/webapp (scripts/i18n-pwa.mjs)
the recovery page, localised at runtime from i18n/webapp (scripts/i18n-pwa.mjs, recovery/recoveryI18n.js)
